set.body: The dry run is the only warning before a sync rewrites fields on a ticket somebody else filed, and it prints those warnings only for items it would update. An item it would close returns early, so its overwrites are never shown. This is the exact case that recently rewrote another reporter's issue title, and had that item been closing rather than updating the dry run would have stayed silent.
set.title: Sync's dry run does not report the field overwrites a close would make

set.body: The Codex package currently carries skills and no lifecycle hooks, on the stated grounds that the two hosts use incompatible hook schemas and that Codex lacks a plan-approval event. Codex in fact supports the prompt-submit, stop, session-start, session-end and post-tool events, and reads the same output shape the existing hooks already emit. Until they ship, a Codex user gets written policy where a Claude user gets enforcement.

set.body: When a compaction lands mid-branch, the rescue re-emits the branch's own events with fresh identifiers so the snapshot cannot overwrite them. Those identifiers sort by time, so a re-emitted early event lands above a later event that was not re-emitted, and the older state wins. Observed on the Codex packaging branch: an item that read done before the merge read in_progress after it, with no warning and no lost events. The rescue should re-emit an item's whole surviving history in its original order, or refuse to re-emit an event older than one it is leaving in place.
set.title: merge-rescue can invert an item's state

set.resolution: Native Codex plugin: manifest, skills, and the prompt/stop/session hooks. Plan capture stays policy-driven because Codex has no ExitPlanMode tool.

set.body: The dispatcher test file has its run-as-a-script block in the middle rather than at the end. Running the file exits at that point, so every class defined below it is never registered and never runs: twenty tests execute where twenty-seven exist. The hidden ones cover overwrite reporting, including the dry-run case, which is the warning that stands between a sync and rewriting a ticket somebody else filed. Continuous integration runs these files as scripts, so it has been reporting green on tests it never executed.
set.title: A stray main block hides seven dispatcher tests

set.body: Release the Codex plugin work and the three correctness fixes found by using the tooling on itself: the merge rescue that could invert an item's state, the sync dry run that was silent about the fields a close would overwrite, and the seven dispatcher tests that never ran.
